theory.intro: A formula links several pronumerals. **Rearranging** it means making a different pronumeral the **subject** — the letter alone on the left, with everything else on the right.
facts: When the subject appears once, isolate it with inverse operations, exactly as when solving an equation.
Undo the operations one at a time, applying the **same** inverse to both sides so the formula stays balanced.
When the subject is multiplied by several things, divide by **all** of them at once: $C=2\pi r$ gives $r=\frac{C}{2\pi}$.
A subtract-then-divide keeps the **whole** numerator over the divisor: $v=u+at$ gives $a=\frac{v-u}{t}$, not $v-\frac{u}{t}$.

To free a squared subject, first isolate the squared term, undoing any addition or subtraction and any multiplication or division, then take square roots. Include $\pm$ when either sign is possible: $A=\pi r^{2}$ gives $r=\pm\sqrt{\frac{A}{\pi}}$.
When the subject is in the **denominator**, multiply both sides by it to bring it up, then isolate it: $P=\frac{F}{A}$ gives $A=\frac{F}{P}$.
Do not divide by zero. Use the positive root for a stated positive quantity. A zero square root gives $0$.
steps: Identify the operations applied to the required subject.
Apply inverse operations to both sides to undo them.
Write the formula with the subject on the left.

workedExamples.question_text:
Make the indicated pronumeral the subject.
a) $N=abp$; make $p$ the subject.
b) $Y=5(3x-7)$; make $x$ the subject.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) Divide both sides by $ab$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{N}{ab}&=p\\p&=\frac{N}{ab}\end{align*}$
b) Divide by $5$, then add $7$ and divide by $3$.
$\begin{align*}\frac{Y}{5}&=3x-7\\\frac{Y}{5}+7&=3x\\x&=\frac{\frac{Y}{5}+7}{3}\end{align*}$

Multiply both sides by $x$, then divide by $y$.
$\begin{align*}xy&=11\\x&=\frac{11}{y}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Make the indicated pronumeral the subject.
a) $Y=7z^{2}+11$; make $z$ the subject.
b) $W=5q^{3}-13$; make $q$ the subject.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) Subtract $11$, then divide by $7$ and take square roots.
$\begin{align*}Y-11&=7z^{2}\\\frac{Y-11}{7}&=z^{2}\\z&=\pm\sqrt{\frac{Y-11}{7}}\end{align*}$
b) Add $13$, then divide by $5$ and take the cube root.
$\begin{align*}W+13&=5q^{3}\\\frac{W+13}{5}&=q^{3}\\q&=\sqrt[3]{\frac{W+13}{5}}\end{align*}$

Divide by $3$, then square both sides.
$\begin{align*}\frac{p}{3}&=\sqrt{5q+7}\\\frac{p^{2}}{9}&=5q+7\\\frac{p^{2}}{9}-7&=5q\\q&=\frac{\frac{p^{2}}{9}-7}{5}\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text:
Make the indicated pronumeral the subject.
a) $H=k+bc$; make $k$ the subject.
b) $J=\frac{z}{de}$; make $z$ the subject.
c) $B=6w+9$; make $w$ the subject.
workedExamples.solution_text:
a) Subtract $bc$ from both sides.
$\begin{align*}H-bc&=k\\k&=H-bc\end{align*}$
b) Multiply both sides by $de$.
$\begin{align*}Jde&=z\\z&=Jde\end{align*}$
c) Subtract $9$, then divide by $6$.
$\begin{align*}B-9&=6w\\\frac{B-9}{6}&=w\\w&=\frac{B-9}{6}\end{align*}$

Multiply by $8$, then take square roots before isolating $x$.
$\begin{align*}8y&=(5x-2)^{2}\\\pm\sqrt{8y}&=5x-2\\2\pm\sqrt{8y}&=5x\\x&=\frac{2\pm\sqrt{8y}}{5}\end{align*}$

development.question_text:
The formula converting Celsius to Fahrenheit is $F=\frac{9}{5}C+32$.
Make $C$ the subject.

mastery.question_text:
The period of a pendulum is $T=2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$.
Make $L$ the subject.
